ai.description: The Nepal Pitviper reaches 60–80 cm. It is bright green with a distinct white or yellow lateral stripe and a reddish-brown tail. Key features include a triangular head and vertical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Trimeresurus septentrionalis* is best distinguished by its distinct, thin white or yellowish postocular stripe that runs along the lower edge of the supraoculars.
ai.habitat: The Nepal Pitviper inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,600 meters across the Himalayan foothills.
ai.behavior: The Nepal pitviper is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting for small vertebrates among the dense foliage of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus septentrionalis* is ovoviviparous, typically producing a litter of 4–12 neonates. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with births recorded in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nepal Pitviper occurs in the Himalayan foothills of northern India, spanning from Himachal Pradesh to Arunachal Pradesh at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
